messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Portuguese, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Portuguese line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
esta me impôs tanta gravidade com o medo que surgia da sua vista, que perdi a esperança da altura.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑by‑Word Mapping (Step 3)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word/Phrase (Portuguese) | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------|------------------------|--------| | **questa** | female agent who acts | **esta** | “this (she)” | OK | | **mi** | recipient/experiencer of the caused state | **me** | “me” | OK | | **porse** | “caused”, act of bringing about a feeling | **impôs** | “imposed / caused” | OK | | **tanto** | high degree of the following noun | **tanta** | “so much” (feminine) | OK | | **di** (line 52) | preposition linking quantity to noun (“of”) | — (omitted) | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | **gravezza** | the affective state “heaviness” | **gravidade** | “heaviness / gravity” | OK | | **con** | preposition “with” introducing an accompanying circumstance | **com** | “with” | OK | | **la** | definite article marking a specific noun | **o** | “the” (masc.) | OK | | **paura** | emotion “fear” that arises from seeing her | **medo** | “fear” | OK | | **ch'uscia** | relative clause verb “that came out / emerged” | **que surgia** | “that emerged” | OK | | **di** (line 53) | preposition “from” indicating source | **da** | “from” | OK | | **sua** | possessive adjective “her” | **sua** | “her” | OK | | **vista** | “sight” – the visual perception of the female agent | **vista** | “sight” | OK | | **ch'io** | relative pronoun introducing the clause “that I …” | **que** | “that” | OK | | **perdei** | “lost” – act of no longer possessing | **perdi** | “lost” | OK | | **la** | definite article marking a specific noun | **a** | “the” (fem.) | OK | | **speranza** | mental expectation “hope” | **esperança** | “hope” | OK | | **de** | preposition “of” linking hope to its content | **da** | “of” | OK | | **l'altezza** | metaphorical “height” – lofty goal | **altura** | “height” | OK |
### Issues Detected - **UNNECESSARY**: *di* (line 52) – the Italian preposition “di” is not required in Portuguese because the noun *gravidade* can stand without a linking preposition in this construction.
No other missing, wrong, or grammatical problems were found.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words.
